short_answer: Jack Jones is a real, long running name in the pick selling business. Saved copies of BetFirms.com show him posting free picks there in 2009 and 2011, and on 17 Nov 2026 BetFirm.com, CappersPicks, Capper Reviews and SportsCapping all sold or promoted his packages. We found no street address or company filing for him.

The sales pages lead with a run of "7314-6415" over the last 3,354 days, about 53.3% winners. The network that sells him also publishes a leaderboard, and its all time line for him is 12,722 wins and 11,505 losses, 52.5%, with a return of about 1% on money risked. In 2026 so far it shows him 904-811-37, 52.7%, roughly break even. The advertised "757-648 Run" since 11 Feb 2026 skips a 147-163 start to the year.

His strongest area on that leaderboard is the NBA, where he ranks first all time at 3,445-2,959-100, 53.8%. Some ranking claims on the sales pages do not match the leaderboard on the same day: "No. 2" overall shows as No. 3, and "No. 2 NFL" shows as No. 5.
Buyer talk outside the network is thin: one 2026 forum exchange shows one member praising a hot NBA day and another calling him mediocre over time. We found no complaints about billing or refunds.

guarantee: The CappersPicks page says most day passes are "GUARANTEED PROFITS" or the next period of picks "is ON JACK." That means more picks, not money. The 3 day pass and the season passes carry no guarantee wording.

SportsCapping, which runs checkout, says on its current Profit Guarantee page that a guaranteed package finishing at zero profit or less ("breaking even counts") earns the next day of picks free, a guaranteed subscription "is automatically extended by its original length," some accounts get account credit instead, "Season and rest-of-season passes are not guaranteed," and "Guarantees apply once per purchase."
The older policy page on Capper Reviews, part of the same network, adds grading on 100 unit intervals whatever the star rating, and says: "We do not offer a money back policy like some services do."
Losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and they are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: How we checked: SportsCapping, the network that sells and grades his picks, publishes a leaderboard by sport and period. We read it on 17 Nov 2026. Its "profit" and ROI columns are the network's own; ROI 0.0102 means about 1 cent returned per dollar risked.

The window effect: the sales run of 7,314 wins and 6,415 losses covers the last 3,354 days, roughly since September 2017. Taking it away from the all time line leaves about 5,400 wins and 5,090 losses before that window, about 51.5%, if both figures count the same picks. The run is accurate for the window, but the window starts where the record looks best. SportsCapping's own method note says a "since" figure is "a window starting on the date shown, not a lifetime record."

Numbers drift between pages read the same day. The overall run appears as 7314-6415 and 7334-6415; the NBA run as 3310-2821 and 3283-2787; the college hoops run as 2363-2134 and 2351-2120. On 17 Nov 2026 the CappersPicks header said $311,670 for $1,000 players; an earlier reading of the same page that day showed 7328-6405 and $316,900.

In the last 90 days the leaderboard shows him 249-216-8 across all sports (53.6%), 46-38-2 in the NFL this season and 89-70-2 in college football this season, all profitable. The CappersPicks "Yesterday's plays" table for 16 Nov 2026 showed 2 wins and 3 losses, $140 down at $100 a play.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: no third party log. We found no outside tracker, contest record, court case or regulator action about him.

What the seller side publishes: long runs by sport, rankings and a yesterday table on the storefronts, plus a leaderboard on SportsCapping. The leaderboard is kept by the network that sells his picks, so it is not an audit, but it is more complete than the runs: 24,739 graded picks all time at 52.5% and about 1% ROI.
CappersPicks labels the network's figures "3RD PARTY DOCUMENTED STATS," but SportsCapping sells his packages and grades them, so they are not third party in the usual sense.

Background: CappersPicks lists his company as Betfirms with the phone line 877-OUR-PICK. The betfirms.com domain was registered on 27 Dec 2003; saved copies from 2009 and 2011 show Jack Jones writing daily free picks there, and it now forwards to BetFirm.com, which on 17 Nov 2026 led with "IF YOU AREN'T WINNING, YOU DON'T KNOW JACK" and linked to the SportsCapping podcast. The CappersPicks footer says the storefront is "located in Antigua, West Indies."

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Jack Jones pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Jack Jones performs beyond what the selling network publishes.
our_data.context: For scale: the selling network's all time line for him is 52.5% winners and its 2026 line 52.7%. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Jack Jones is thin. The largest set of comments sits on a site that says it is part of the network selling his picks. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found very little buyer talk about Jack Jones outside the sites that sell him. The main pool is 11 undated comments on Capper Reviews, a network owned site, and all of them are favorable: buyers praise early releases, detailed write ups and leaderboard finishes. Outside the network, members of TheRX repost his paid plays; in one April 2026 thread they tallied a 6 and 1 day and one called it an NBA heater, while another member wrote that over time he is mediocre and asked for proof from an independent monitor. Reddit archive searches and our saved copy of ten betting subreddits found no posts about the handicapper. The BBB has no listing for SportsCapping. We found no complaints about billing or refunds, and no independent long term record either way.

Capper Reviews shows a rating of 3.71 out of 5 from 142 votes and 11 undated comments. All are favorable, mentioning college hoops, an NBA call, an opening day baseball underdog, a winning Sunday and his long write ups; one tells readers to follow BetFirm. The page says Jack Jones sells picks through the SportsCapping network, which Capper Reviews is part of, so this is not independent evidence.

In the TheRX Sunday service play thread for 5 Apr 2026, members who repost paid plays tallied his card from that day as 6 and 0 in the NBA and 0 and 1 in baseball, and one said he was on an NBA heater. This is one day of results.

In the same thread another member answered that, from what he had seen and read over time, Jack Jones is "quite mediocre," and said only documentation from an objective monitoring service, not the seller's own site, would change his view. He gave no numbers.

In the TheRX Saturday service play thread for 14 Nov 2026, a member reposted seven of his plays rated 20 to 25 units, with no comment on results. Unlike Sean Murphy and several network cappers, Jack Jones is not on that forum's do not post list.

Reddit archive searches for Jack Jones in the main betting subreddits returned no posts about the handicapper; the few matches in r/sportsbook were about other people. Our web searches found no Sportsbook Review or Covers thread reviewing his service.
A BBB search for SportsCapping, the network that sells his packages, returned no business, so there is no BBB complaint history to read.

conflicts: Capper Reviews, which hosts the star rating and comments, and the leaderboard that ranks him are both run by the SportsCapping network that sells his packages and takes a share of each sale.

The Capper Reviews page carried a "$1,000 Free Play at MyBookie" banner linked through an affiliate tracking address. MyBookie is an offshore sportsbook, not licensed by U.S. state regulators. Affiliate deals usually pay the referrer when referred customers sign up or lose.
CappersPicks calls the network's figures third party documented stats, and its footer says the site is "located in Antigua, West Indies."
SportsCapping's About page says "No cherry-picked highlights," while the package copy it sells leads with runs whose start dates are chosen.
strengths: A long running, named seller: archived pages show him publishing picks under the BetFirms name since at least 2009.
The network's own leaderboard, though kept by the seller side, shows a positive all time line (52.5%, about 1% ROI) over a very large sample, and first place all time in the NBA.
Prices are published for every package, from $34.95 for one play up.
The guarantee rules are written out in detail, and the yesterday table shows losing days, not only wins.
Recent form on the leaderboard is positive: 249-216-8 over the last 90 days.
concerns: No independent record. Every number comes from the network that sells and grades the picks.
The headline runs start on chosen dates; the full 2026 line is 52.7% and roughly break even, and the all time return is about 1%.
Several ranking claims did not match the network's own leaderboard on the same day, and run totals differ between pages.
The guarantee gives more picks, never money back, and season passes have no guarantee.
No street address found; the storefront footer gives Antigua, and the rating page carries an offshore sportsbook affiliate banner.
At about 1% return on money risked, small differences in the line you get can erase the edge.
checklist: Open the SportsCapping leaderboard, set it to All Time and This Season, and compare with the runs on the package you are about to buy.
Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A long run on a sales page is not a record.
Count units, not wins. About 52.5% winners is close to break even once you bet at worse lines than the page uses.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Here every version is free time or credit, and season passes have none.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, long running seller whose packages have published prices on established storefronts. The selling network's own leaderboard shows him slightly profitable over the long run, about 1% ROI, but no independent party has audited his record, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
Who is Jack Jones and what is BetFirm?

His bio says he was a private consultant to bigger players before going public in 2008. CappersPicks lists his company as Betfirms, and saved BetFirms.com pages from 2009 and 2011 show him posting free picks there. BetFirms.com now forwards to BetFirm.com, a picks site built around him that links to the SportsCapping network.
How much does Jack Jones cost?
On 17 Nov 2026 single plays were $34.95 and $39.95, a 1 day all sports pass was $59.95, 30 days $399.95, 90 days $999.95 and 365 days $1,999.95. Season passes ran from $499.95 to $1,199.95.
No cash refunds. Most day passes carry a guarantee of more picks if they do not profit, the 3 day pass and season passes carry none, and the network says it does not offer a money back policy.
Does Jack Jones have a verified record?

No independent one. The network that sells him grades his picks and shows 12,722-11,505-512 all time, 52.5%, and 904-811-37 so far in 2026. The bigger runs on his sales pages start on dates the seller chose.

You get every play released in the period you buy, and on most day passes a free repeat period if it loses. His long run edge on the seller's own numbers is about 1% of money risked, which is easy to lose to worse lines, and nothing refunds the package or your betting losses.
